name: St. Peter's Catholic Church
history: The first resident priest came to Columbia in 1820, and the parish's first church, designed by South Carolina architect Robert Mills, was finished in 1824. The present church, by Frank Pierce Milburn, was built from 1906 to 1908 and dedicated in January 1909. In 2018 it became the first basilica in South Carolina.
arch: Gothic Revival in dark red brick with Bedford limestone and glazed terra cotta trim. Its spire and cross rise 163 feet.
features: Its 3,500-pound bell was cast in 1911 by the McShane Bell Foundry of Baltimore.
It is the oldest Catholic parish in Columbia and the Midlands.

look.d: The spire rises over Assembly Street, near the State House.
The trim is dull-glazed terra cotta set in red brick.

fun: The first church's architect, Robert Mills, later designed the Washington Monument.
journal: South Carolina's first basilica. Red brick and a 3,500-pound voice in the tower.

quiz.q: What was it the first of in South Carolina?
